title: China’s iSpace raises first batch of series E funding for reusable rocketry
summary: China's iSpace has secured the first batch of Series E funding for its reusable rocketry efforts, with additional fundraising still ongoing. This follows a significant D++ funding round completed earlier.

title: One species, one planet: The moon is our ethical dress rehearsal for Mars
summary: The article discusses how the Moon serves as an ethical rehearsal for future human missions to Mars, highlighting the pragmatic systems engineering work of Bruce Jakosky, Scott Hubbard, and their team. Their recent editorial emphasizes the importance of lunar exploration in preparing for Mars missions.

title: Firefly increases vehicle production even as launches lag
summary: Firefly Aerospace is increasing production of its launch vehicles due to strong interest, but this has not yet resulted in a higher launch rate.

title: U.S. expands missile production as Army seeks more depth in its arsenal
summary: The U.S. is increasing missile production to enhance its arsenal, with recent agreements involving Northrop, Lockheed, and L3Harris to expand capacity in propulsion, structures, and other critical supply chain areas.

title: Golden Dome faces 2027 funding cliff
summary: The Golden Dome program is at risk of losing funding by 2027, with Gen. Michael Guetlein urging Congress to secure future financing as most initial funds are already allocated. The program's next phase remains uncertain without additional financial commitments.

title: National lab visit boosts NASA’s confidence in space nuclear propulsion mission
summary: NASA officials expressed confidence in launching a nuclear electric propulsion demonstration mission by the end of 2028 after visiting a national lab constructing the mission's reactor. The visit reinforced their belief in the project's feasibility.

title: Golden Dome money starting to reach contractors, but long-term funding still unclear
summary: Pentagon contractors are starting to receive funding related to the Golden Dome program, though much of it is channeled through existing programs. The long-term funding situation for the initiative remains uncertain.

title: Webinar on MOSA Interoperability Standards for Space Systems – August 26, 2026
summary: The MOSA Interface Standards Alliance is hosting a webinar on August 26, 2026, to discuss MOSA interoperability standards for space systems. The event aims to bring together industry stakeholders to explore standardization in space technology.

title: TechnoMile’s Five-Year Sustained Growth Recognized with  Place on the 2026 Inc. 5000 List
summary: TechnoMile has been ranked No. 4,268 on the 2026 Inc. 5000 list, recognizing its five-year sustained growth. The company is a leading AI solution provider for growth, contracts, compliance, and security workflows.

title: SpaceX increasing footprint in missile defense
summary: SpaceX is expanding its role in missile defense by securing multibillion-dollar contracts for satellite networks, sensing, and launch services, leveraging its vertically integrated manufacturing model to compete for Pentagon contracts.

title: SpaceX wraps Starlink double header day with the launch of 24 Starlink satellites from California
summary: SpaceX successfully launched 24 Starlink satellites from California on Aug. 11, completing the second Starlink mission of the day.

title: A total solar eclipse will darken the sky for millions today! Here's what you need to know
summary: A total solar eclipse will occur today, passing over Greenland, Iceland, and Spain. Details on timings, livestreams, and safety advice are available.

title: SpaceX could make $500 billion in 2028, Elon Musk says (video)
summary: Elon Musk predicts SpaceX could generate $500 billion in revenue by 2028, highlighting the company's shift from launch services to artificial intelligence. The transition positions SpaceX for significant financial growth in the coming years.

title: Scientists create largest 2D map of the universe with 5.6 trillion pixels and nearly 4 billion cosmic objects
summary: Scientists have developed the largest 2D map of the universe, consisting of 5.6 trillion pixels and encompassing nearly 4 billion cosmic objects. This map is expected to become a foundational resource for future astronomical research.

title: Scientists find 2 million active black holes, exploding stars and more, nearly doubling our view of the high-energy universe
summary: Astronomers have nearly doubled the number of known cosmic X-ray sources, identifying 2 million active black holes and exploding stars. This discovery significantly expands our view of the high-energy universe.

title: 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds': Anson Mount, Rebecca Romijn, & Carol Kane on season 4's big leaps and 'outside the box' episodes
summary: The producers of 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' had more time to prepare for season 4, resulting in incredible episodes. The cast discusses the show's creative direction and 'outside the box' storytelling.

title: 1-billion-year-old Mars meteorite found in Algeria is like nothing we've seen from the Red Planet
summary: Scientists discovered a 1-billion-year-old Mars meteorite in Algeria, providing new insights into the Red Planet's geological history. This meteorite is unlike any previously studied Martian samples, filling a significant gap in our understanding of Mars' past.

title: SpaceX launches 29 Starlink satellites to orbit from Florida (video, photos)
summary: SpaceX launched 29 Starlink satellites into orbit from Florida's Space Coast. This mission expands the company's growing constellation of internet satellites.

title: NASA will chase the Aug. 12 total solar eclipse with balloons and a high-altitude jet
summary: NASA plans to observe the August 12 total solar eclipse using balloons and a high-altitude jet to study the sun's corona. This approach offers unique insights not possible from other locations in the solar system.

title: Starbase Production lining up future vehicles
summary: SpaceX's Starbase production site is progressing with the assembly of multiple Starship vehicles. This indicates ongoing preparations for future missions and testing.

title: Launch Preview: Chinese failure opens busy international launch salvo
summary: The week of August 10 started with four launches across three countries following a Chinese launch failure. This event highlights a busy period in international space launches.

title: Artemis progress building lunar return roadmap
summary: NASA has released updates on the Artemis program, detailing progress in building a roadmap for returning humans to the Moon. The updates include plans for commercial robotic lunar missions.

title: Blue Origin working engine resolutions and dual pad future
summary: Blue Origin is nearing the end of its investigation into a catastrophic engine explosion. The company is also planning for a dual-pad future.

title: Relativity Space engine integration milestone for Terran-R first stage
summary: Relativity Space has achieved a key milestone in integrating engines for the first stage of its reusable Terran-R rocket. This progress marks a significant advancement in the development of the rocket.

title: Crew-13 pilot reflects on career, training, and upcoming science ahead of flight to ISS
summary: NASA has moved up the launch date for the Crew-13 mission to the ISS. The Crew-13 pilot shared insights on their career, training, and the upcoming scientific objectives of the mission.

title: While SpaceX recovers Ship 40, Ship 41 prepares for testing ahead of Flight 14
summary: SpaceX is recovering Ship 40 after its soft landing in the Indian Ocean, while Ship 41 prepares for testing ahead of Flight 14.

title: Launch Preview: Starlink, AST SpaceMobile, and Chinese missions fill launch manifest
summary: The first full week of August is expected to be busy for space launches, with Starlink, AST SpaceMobile, and multiple Chinese missions scheduled. This highlights the growing activity in commercial and international spaceflight.

title: Boeing’s Starliner set for potential 2026 cargo run to ISS
summary: Boeing's CST-100 Starliner spacecraft may conduct a cargo mission to the ISS in 2026, with CEO Kelly Ortberg highlighting ongoing redesign efforts.

title: Starbase Pad 1 Retrofits Progress as Block 3 Flights Start
summary: SpaceX has completed two flights from the newly designed Pad 2 at Starbase, while retrofitting work continues on Pad 1 for Block 3 flights. The progress at Starbase highlights SpaceX's ongoing infrastructure upgrades for future missions.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates 50 years with a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements. The publication marks five decades of significant contributions in space exploration and technology.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial eclipses and computer simulations to observe the Sun's corona. This approach allows scientists to gather more data than during natural eclipses, which are brief and rare.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: The European Space Agency is inviting European researchers and companies to test their software aboard the Hera mission, which will travel millions of kilometers into deep space. This initiative provides a unique opportunity to run experiments in a real deep-space environment.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESTEC, the European Space Agency’s technical centre in the Netherlands. This marks a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will use a coronagraph to study the Sun's corona by blocking out the Sun's bright disk, creating an artificial eclipse. This technique allows for detailed observations of the solar atmosphere.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event on 16–17 September at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands will bring together startups and space industry leaders to exchange ideas, showcase capabilities, and explore collaborations.

title: The silicon brains steering next-generation antennas
summary: The article discusses advancements in silicon-based technology for next-generation antennas, highlighting their role in steering and improving antenna performance. This innovation is poised to enhance communication systems in the space industry.

title: Plato's electronics ready for space
summary: ESA's Plato spacecraft has completed key electromagnetic compatibility tests in the Maxwell Test Chamber, ensuring its electronics are space-ready. The mission is scheduled to launch on an Ariane 6 rocket in March 2027.

title: Test firing at brand new green chemical propulsion lab
summary: A new green chemical propulsion lab conducted its first test firing. This marks a significant step in developing environmentally friendly propulsion technologies for space missions.

title: Firefly Announces Record Q2 Results
summary: Firefly Aerospace reported its first-ever quarterly revenue exceeding $100 million, driven by new launch and defense contracts. The company announced these record Q2 results on Tuesday.

title: Guetlein: CR Could Mean ‘No Golden Dome…No Funding’
summary: A senior official warned that a Continuing Resolution (CR) could lead to the cancellation of the 'Golden Dome' project due to lack of funding. The statement underscores the financial risks posed by budget delays.

title: Bill Spotlight: Space Superiority Readiness Act
summary: A bipartisan group of senators introduced a bill to ensure U.S. military readiness for potential space conflicts with China. The legislation aims to enhance space superiority capabilities.

title: Rocket Lab Unveils GHOST on a Record Quarter
summary: Rocket Lab introduced GHOST, a deployable launch system for responsive global launches. The announcement coincided with a record quarter for the company.

title: Astrolight, ATMOS Partner on Laser Comms Reentry Demo
summary: Astrolight and ATMOS have partnered to conduct a laser communications demonstration during ATMOS' PHOENIX 2 reentry vehicle mission in 2027. This collaboration aims to advance reentry communication technologies using laser terminals.

title: MDA Space Will ‘Repurpose’ Canadarm3 For Lunar Surface
summary: MDA Space plans to adapt its Canadarm3 robotics technology for lunar surface operations following NASA's pause on the Gateway program. The company aims to leverage its microgravity robot-arm expertise for new lunar missions.

title: Europe’s IRIS2 Constellation Enters the Build Phase
summary: Europe's IRIS2 constellation has entered the build phase after seven months of negotiations among the European Commission, ESA, EUSPA, and SpaceRISE. The implementation phase marks a significant milestone for the project.

title: The Launch Crunch Just Made a ULA Sale Worth Revisiting
summary: The launch industry's high demand has made ULA's potential sale more attractive. This comes as the space sector faces a significant increase in launch activity.

title: Redwire Books Starfall’s First Dedicated Mission
summary: Redwire subsidiary SpaceMD secured a contract to transport up to 32 mini-labs on a future SpaceX Starfall mission. This marks the first dedicated mission under Redwire's Starfall program.

title: Op-ed: Aging Weather Satellites Are Raising Risks for America. It’s Time for a Hybrid Solution.
summary: Aging weather satellites are increasing risks for the U.S., prompting calls for a hybrid solution to improve military weather data quality. The op-ed emphasizes the need for enhanced satellite capabilities to maintain strategic advantages.

title: Rocket Lab Margins Under the Microscope Following 2Q Earnings
summary: Rocket Lab faced investor scrutiny over its margins following the release of its second quarter earnings. The company's financial performance became a focal point for analysts and investors.

title: DamoTech Joins Space ISAC
summary: DamoTech has joined the Space Information Sharing and Analysis Center (Space ISAC), specializing in advanced cybersecurity for the space sector.

title: U.S. Space Force Selects Voyager Technologies for Space-to-Space Communications Development Award
summary: The U.S. Space Force has selected Voyager Technologies to develop space-to-space communication capabilities under a new contract. The award aims to enhance communication systems for the Space Force's Space Systems Command.

title: The Trump Administration Attempts to Fill an Empty FCC Seat Ahead of Midterm Elections
summary: The Trump Administration nominated FCC Chairman Brendan Carr’s replacement to fill an empty seat at the Federal Communications Commission ahead of midterm elections. This move aims to restore the FCC to a full four-member panel after nearly two years with only three members.

title: Arabsat Signs Digital Communications Infrastructure Deal with Libya Telecom and Technology (LTT)
summary: Arabsat has signed a deal with Libya Telecom and Technology (LTT) to develop Libya's digital communications infrastructure. The agreement aims to enhance connectivity for Libya's population of around 7.5 million people.

title: ALL.SPACE to Provide Hydra MAX Terminals to Aalyria
summary: ALL.SPACE has secured a contract to supply Hydra MAX terminals to Aalyria for integration with Spacetime orchestration software. The deployment will enhance Aalyria's satellite communication capabilities.

title: Catalyst Completes Infrastructure EO Analysis Pilot Program with UK Rail Operator
summary: Catalyst, a subsidiary of PCI Geomatics, completed a 12-week pilot program with Network Rail to analyze weather-driven risks using Earth Observation (EO) analytics. The program aimed to assess infrastructure vulnerabilities in Britain's railway network.

title: SES, Eutelsat Complete RDV1 Milestone for Europe’s IRIS2 Sovereign Constellation Program
summary: SES and Eutelsat have achieved the RDV1 milestone for Europe's IRIS² sovereign constellation program. This marks a significant step in the implementation phase of the satellite initiative.

title: CEO Fallacher Suggests Eutelsat is ‘Undervalued’ Compared to SpaceX Following 2025-26 Results
summary: Eutelsat's CEO Fallacher claims the company is undervalued compared to SpaceX following strong growth in its LEO business segment in the 2025-2026 fiscal year. The report highlights Eutelsat's performance in the satellite industry.

title: How the Internet of Space is Reshaping Active Resiliency
summary: Satellite data has long been crucial for disaster assessment and emergency response. The 'Internet of Space' is now enhancing active resiliency in these areas.
